subject: Chemistry

stem: For the ion 81Br-, how many protons, neutrons and electrons are present?
solution: Bromine has atomic number 35; neutrons=81-35; the -1 ion has 36 electrons.

stem: A gas occupies 1.50 dm3 at 100 kPa and 300 K. What volume will it occupy at 150 kPa and 330 K?
What is the ground-state electron configuration of Fe2+?
solution: The 4s electrons are removed before 3d electrons.

stem: A compound contains 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?
solution: Mole ratio is approximately 3.33:6.7:3.33 = 1:2:1.

stem: Which combination is expected for solid and molten sodium oxide?

options.html: The solid does not conduct; the melt conducts.
Both solid and melt conduct by mobile electrons.
The solid conducts; the melt does not.
Neither conducts because all bonds are covalent.

solution: Ions are fixed in the solid and mobile in the melt.

stem: What are the electron-domain geometry and molecular geometry of SF4?
solution: Five domains include one lone pair.

stem: In which species is a coordinate covalent bond formed when the species is produced?
solution: Nitrogen donates both electrons in the new N-H bond.

stem: Which molecule is polar?
solution: Its tetrahedral bond dipoles do not cancel.

stem: How many sigma and pi bonds are present in propene, CH2=CHCH3?
solution: Six C-H sigma plus two C-C sigma; one pi in the double bond.

stem: Which set correctly classifies Rb, Ni, I and Ne?

options.html: Transition element, alkali metal, noble gas, halogen.
Alkali metal, transition element, halogen, noble gas.
Halogen, transition element, alkali metal, noble gas.
Alkali metal, halogen, transition element, noble gas.

solution: The elements occupy groups 1, d-block, 17 and 18 respectively.

stem: Which oxide produces the solution with the highest pH when equal amounts react fully with water?
solution: Potassium oxide forms strongly alkaline KOH.

stem: Which functional groups occur in CH3COOCH2CH2NH2?
solution: The structure contains -COO- and -NH2.

stem: Which pair consists of functional-group isomers?
solution: Both have formula C3H6O but aldehyde/ketone groups.

stem: Why do many transition-metal complexes absorb visible light?

options.html: Their nuclei emit visible photons during radioactive decay.
Ligands split d orbitals so electrons can absorb specific photon energies.
All ligands contain delocalized pi electrons.
Metal ions have completely filled d subshells.

solution: d-d transitions can lie in the visible range.

stem: Which compound can show E/Z isomerism?
solution: Each alkene carbon has two different substituents.

stem: A molecular ion peak occurs at m/z 74 and a strong fragment occurs at m/z 31. Which compound is most consistent?
solution: A CH2OH+ fragment at 31 is characteristic of a primary alcohol; M=74.

stem: In Zn(s)+Cu2+(aq) -> Zn2+(aq)+Cu(s), which statement is correct?

options.html: Zinc is oxidized and is the reducing agent.
Copper(II) is oxidized and is the reducing agent.
Zinc gains electrons and is reduced.

solution: Zn loses electrons, causing reduction of Cu2+.

stem: What is the sum of coefficients when C3H8 is completely combusted using smallest whole numbers?
solution: C3H8+5O2 -> 3CO2+4H2O; sum=13.

stem: Given H2+1/2O2 -> H2O, delta H=-286 kJ mol-1, what is delta H for 2H2O -> 2H2+O2?
solution: Reverse and double the equation.

stem: Which change has a negative entropy change?
solution: Gas particle number decreases from three to two.

stem: How does increasing temperature change a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution?

options.html: The peak becomes lower and shifts to higher energy.
The peak becomes higher and shifts to lower energy.
The distribution becomes narrower with the same mean.
The fraction above activation energy always decreases.

solution: Higher temperature broadens the distribution and raises mean energy.

stem: 1.20 g Mg reacts with 100.0 cm3 of 0.400 mol dm-3 HCl. What remains when reaction stops?

options.html: Magnesium remains and all HCl is used.

solution: n(Mg)=0.0494 mol; n(HCl)=0.0400 mol, enough for only 0.0200 mol Mg.

stem: Which change decreases the initial rate of reaction between marble chips and hydrochloric acid?

options.html: Using larger marble chips at the same mass.

solution: Larger pieces have lower surface area.

stem: For N2(g)+3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g), delta H<0, which change increases equilibrium yield of NH3?

options.html: Adding a catalyst and increasing temperature.

solution: Products have fewer gas moles and the forward reaction is exothermic.

stem: For an equilibrium, K increases when temperature increases. What follows?

options.html: Products must have fewer gas molecules.

solution: Heat acts as a reactant for an endothermic forward process.

stem: What is represented by the Arrhenius pre-exponential factor A?
solution: A includes frequency and steric probability.

stem: Which electrodes are most suitable for electrolysing aqueous copper(II) sulfate without introducing new reacting species?
solution: Graphite is relatively inert under these conditions.

stem: Which 0.10 mol dm-3 solution is expected to have pH above 7?
solution: Ethanoate is the conjugate base of a weak acid.

stem: In F2+2Br- -> 2F-+Br2, what is the oxidizing agent?
solution: F2 gains electrons and is reduced.

stem: Which reaction occurs spontaneously under standard conditions?
solution: Chlorine is a stronger oxidizing agent than bromine.

stem: In a Zn/Cu galvanic cell, which statement is correct?

options.html: Electrons flow from copper to zinc externally.
Zinc is the negative anode and copper is the positive cathode.
Zinc ions are reduced at the zinc electrode.

solution: Zn is oxidized at the anode; electrons flow to Cu.

stem: What forms at the electrodes during electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl with inert electrodes?

options.html: Hydrogen at the cathode and chlorine at the anode.

solution: Water is reduced; chloride is oxidized in concentrated brine.

stem: Why is BF3 a Lewis acid?

options.html: It can accept an electron pair into an incomplete valence shell.
It donates a lone pair from boron.
It releases hydroxide ions in water.

solution: Boron has only six valence electrons in BF3.

stem: Which species acts as an electrophile in CH3Br+OH- -> CH3OH+Br-?
solution: The C-Br bond polarizes carbon delta positive.

stem: What is the electrophile in nitration of benzene?
solution: The nitronium ion attacks the aromatic ring.

stem: Which compound undergoes nucleophilic substitution fastest with aqueous hydroxide under comparable conditions?
solution: A tertiary bromoalkane combines a stable carbocation tendency with a weaker C-Br bond.

stem: What is the charge on [Fe(H2O)4(OH)2] if iron is in oxidation state +3?
solution: Water is neutral and two hydroxide ligands total -2; +3-2=+1.

stem: What is the pH of 2.5x10-3 mol dm-3 HNO3?
solution: Strong acid: pH=-log(2.5x10^-3)=2.60.

stem: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 12 min. What fraction remains after 36 min?
solution: 36 min is three half-lives: (1/2)^3.

stem: A compound has a broad IR absorption near 3000 cm-1 and a strong absorption near 1710 cm-1. Which group is most likely present?
solution: Broad O-H plus C=O is characteristic of a carboxylic acid.
